Tuesday, September 9, 2025  7:00 PM  Council Chamber

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's web site under City Council Meeting agendas at www.RollingHillsEstates.gov and
  during regular business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's web
  site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP -TV
  Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to
  address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public comment, please
  complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 9, 2025

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR STEGURA called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR STEGURA.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Attorney Steve McEwen
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development/Public Works Director Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING SEPTEMBER 15- OCTOBER 15 "HISPANIC
  HERITAGE MONTH"

MAYOR STEGURA declared September 15 – October15, 2025 as “Hispanic Heritage
Month.”

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-E AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF AUGUST 2025

  APPROVED WARRANTS 68853 THROUGH 68927 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $415,598.84 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 080425 THROUGH
  080525; 090125 THROUGH 090225; IN THE AMOUNT OF $135,349.05; FOR
  A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT OF $550,947.89 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF AUGUST 4, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

D.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF AUGUST 19, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 9, 2025
 E.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF AUGUST 26, 2025

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Public comment was received from Tom Hyatt on behalf of Fred Brown’s Recovery Services
in San Pedro, discussing expansion plans. Public comment was also received from Merlin
David on behalf of Peninsula Library Friends Foundation, announcing upcoming Hispanic
Heritage Month events.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ELECTRIC VEHICLE PURCHASE USING AQMD FUNDS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the purchase of a 2025 Ford
  Mustang Mach-E all-electric vehicle through the Sourcewell cooperative purchasing
  program in the amount of $53,809.64.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant City Manager Davis explained that there are currently two City vehicles, aside from
maintenance vehicles, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Assistant City Manager Davis outlined how staff arrived on the Ford Mustang Mach-E as a
recommendation, following direction from the City Council during the Policy Development
Session in March, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Discussion ensued on the importance of mileage range in all-electric vehicles.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE THE PURCHASE OF A 2025 FORD MUSTANG MACH-E ALL-
  ELECTRIC VEHICLE THROUGH THE SOURCEWELL COOPERATIVE
  PURCHASING PROGRAM IN THE AMOUNT OF $53,809.64.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  ORDINANCE NO. 754 REPEALING CHAPTER 8.08 OF THE ROLLING HILLS
  MUNICIPAL CODE PERTAINING TO ALARM SYSTEMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Introduce for a first reading, Ordinance
  No. 754; and 2) Direct staff to bring back Ordinance No. 754 for a second reading
  and adoption at the City Council meeting of September 23, 2025.

Community Development & Public Works Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per
the agenda material).

MAYOR STEGURA expressed concern that the removal of the false alarm fines would
potentially increase the burden on the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department who respond
to these alarms.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 9, 2025
   COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  INTRODUCE FOR A FIRST READING, ORDINANCE NO. 754 AND DIRECT
  STAFF TO BRING BACK ORDINANCE NO. 754 FOR A SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION AT THE CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF SEPTEMBER 23,
  2025.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Zerunyan
  NOES:  Stegura
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance 754 by title.

C.  ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 2607 AND APPROVAL OF GRANT AGREEMENT
  WITH THE SAN GABRIEL AND LOWER LOS ANGELES RIVERS AND MOUNTAINS
  CONSERVANCY FOR THE NEW NATURE CENTER AT GEORGE F CANYON
  PROJECT

  Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution No. 2607, certifying the
  approval of the application for Proposition 68 grant funds, providing additional
  certifications as required under the grant program, and authorizing the City Manager
  to execute the Agreement between the City and the San Gabriel and Lower Los
  Angeles Rivers and Mountains Conservancy.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  ZERUNYAN, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2607, CERTIFYING THE APPROVAL OF THE
  APPLICATION FOR PROPOSITION 68 GRANT FUNDS, PROVIDING
  ADDITIONAL CERTIFICATIONS AS REQUIRED UNDER THE GRANT
  PROGRAM, AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE THE
  AGREEMENT BETWEEN THE CITY AND THE SAN GABRIEL AND LOWER
  LOS ANGELES RIVERS AND MOUNTAINS CONSERVANCY.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution 2607 by title.

D.  FOURTH AMENDMENT TO CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Fourth Amendment to City
  Manager Employment Agreement and authorize its execution by the Mayor.

Assistant City Manager McEwen provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE FOURTH AMENDMENT TO CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT
  AGREEMENT AND AUTHORIZE ITS EXECUTION BY THE MAYOR.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 9, 2025
   AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER announced there will be a Traffic & Safety Committee
meeting on September 17.

MAYOR STEGURA noted that Board Alternate Steve Zuckerman attended the Clean Power
Alliance Board meeting last week on her behalf.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR STEGURA announced a location change for the upcoming City Celebration, which
will now take place at Ernie Howlett Park on Saturday, September 13, 2025.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ attended the Portuguese Bend Horse show last weekend and
relayed the compliments she received about City staff’s work in support of the event.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:26 p.m. MAYOR STEGURA adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 23, 2025
at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a regular meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Debby Stegura, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 9, 2025
